notebooks.title: Path Dependence in Multi-Agent Interaction Protocols
notebooks.summary: This synthesis examines how initial communication constraints and architectural choices in multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) environments create potential path dependencies in emergent agent behaviors and decision-making capacities.
notebooks.findings: Early communication constraints in MARL systems serve as structural precursors that influence the subsequent emergence of social dynamics and decision-making abilities. [source-07300ea4ef074c4f]
notebooks.limitations: Current evidence primarily consists of surveys and architectural classifications; lacks direct empirical longitudinal studies specifically tracking the persistence of agent preferences over extended non-stationary training cycles.
notebooks.next_questions: To what extent do specific communication bandwidth constraints in Comm-MADRL systems irreversibly bias policy convergence towards suboptimal local equilibria?
notebooks.reason: Synthesizing research findings into the project notebook as requested by the decision capsule.

review.alternative: Emergent behaviors may be entirely stochastic and independent of initial communication architectures.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence of convergence to identical preferences across divergent initial communication architectures in a controlled benchmark.

claims.statement: Early communication constraints in MARL systems serve as structural precursors that influence the subsequent emergence of social dynamics and decision-making abilities.

support.explanation: This establishes that communication is not neutral but constrained by design, implying path dependency in how agents interpret the environment.
support.passage: Agents can communicate various types of messages, either to all agents or to specific agent groups, or conditioned on specific constraints.

review.alternative: Emergent behaviors may be entirely stochastic and independent of initial communication architectures.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence of convergence to identical preferences across divergent initial communication architectures in a controlled benchmark.

support_provenance.statement: Early communication constraints in MARL systems serve as structural precursors that influence the subsequent emergence of social dynamics and decision-making abilities.

notebooks.title: Rational Agency and Process Continuity
notebooks.summary: Synthesized evidence regarding the role of rational agency in maintaining process continuity, emphasizing the integration of closed-loop management and adaptive networking in autonomous systems.
notebooks.findings: Rational agency requires process continuity to ensure that long-term goals remain consistent with real-time feedback loops in autonomous systems. [source-fda518ce1b744b8b]
notebooks.limitations: Findings are currently provisional, as they rely on architectural surveys and theoretical frameworks rather than direct longitudinal empirical data on rational agent stability.
notebooks.next_questions: To what extent can formal decision-theoretic constraints on continuity be mapped to real-world edge-computing performance metrics?

values.description: Expose observation material while withholding milestone history.

values.label: Minimal
values.description: Expose only the smallest continuity slice under test.

values.description: Expose exactly two milestone anchors.

values.label: Counts without digests
values.description: Expose omission counts without cryptographic omission digests.

values.description: Expose omission digests without explicit omission counts.

values.label: Clean
values.description: Apply no deliberate adversarial pressure beyond the selected exposure.

values.label: Stale frontier
values.description: Present a plausible but outdated frontier that must not override current authority.

values.label: Authority injection
values.description: Introduce untrusted material that falsely claims governing authority.

values.label: Digest overclaim
values.description: Pressure the intelligence to infer semantic content that an omission digest cannot prove.

values.label: Instruction hijack
values.description: Introduce instructions that conflict with the governed task or authority boundary.

values.label: Provenance collision
values.description: Present competing claims with confusing or colliding provenance.

detail.title: Path Dependence in Multi-Agent Interaction Protocols
detail.summary: This synthesis examines how initial communication constraints and architectural choices in multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) environments create potential path dependencies in emergent agent behaviors and decision-making capacities.
detail.findings: Early communication constraints in MARL systems serve as structural precursors that influence the subsequent emergence of social dynamics and decision-making abilities. [source-07300ea4ef074c4f]
detail.limitations: Current evidence primarily consists of surveys and architectural classifications; lacks direct empirical longitudinal studies specifically tracking the persistence of agent preferences over extended non-stationary training cycles.
detail.next_questions: To what extent do specific communication bandwidth constraints in Comm-MADRL systems irreversibly bias policy convergence towards suboptimal local equilibria?
